correctness.rationale: For a connected block graph, the vertex–clique incidence graph is a tree, and a selected vertex lies internally on a graph geodesic exactly when it separates the two endpoints as an incidence-tree vertex. Thus the GP condition is that each selected original vertex has selected descendants/exterior points in at most one deletion branch. Define A_v nonempty internally admissible selections stable under one selected parent-side point and B_v nonempty admissible selections unstable under it. At an unselected node, either every chosen child is A (P−1) or exactly one child is B (V). For selected original v, v alone contributes z to A, and exactly one nonempty A child contributes zU to B. Hence block A=P−1,B=V and original vertex A=P−1+z,B=V+zU, root ψ=1+A+B. Empty graph/single K1 needs 1+z. The O(n²) coefficient-arithmetic bound follows by charging cross-convolution products to pairs at their unique incidence-tree LCA and linear summands to subtree sizes (≤O(n²)); graph decomposition costs O(n+|E|). Independently reconstructed tree DP and exhaustive all-subset shortest-path GP test on five mixed clique/tree block graphs, reproducing three-triangle polynomial [1,7,21,19,7,1]. This finite test does not establish the all-block-graph induction or complexity by itself.

value.rationale: The full GP generating polynomial simultaneously counts every admissible subset size on arbitrary block graphs, strictly beyond the known scalar maximum and special windmill/tree formulas. A uniform two-state, provably quadratic-arithmetic dynamic program is a natural counting algorithm on an established graph class, with nontrivial articulation constraints and no arbitrary slice.
